rationale: THE WRAPPED RECEIVER (C10, 2026-11-25). receiverOwnerType branches on the receiver node's own `type`, so a parenthesis (`(new Worker()).run()`) and a non-null assertion (`w!.run()`) each hid the node underneath: neither matched a branch, neither carried `metadata.owner`, and both fell to the store's NAME model. MEASURED on a three-file repro: `(new Worker()).run()` bound to `other.ts:run` while the caller imports only `Worker`. The rival `Other.run` is load-bearing — without a same-named member in the file the name model resolves correctly and this fixture passes with or without the fix. A CAST is pinned separately and with its own evidence class: `(value as Worker).run()` STATES the type, so the analyzer must report `cast` rather than unwrap the cast away and re-derive the type from `value: unknown`.

expectRelationships.note: THE GAIN: the parenthesis is stripped, so the new_expression underneath states the owner
THE GAIN: `!` asserts presence, it does not change the type, so the parameter's type survives
CONTROL/GUARD: a cast is a STATED type; unwrapping it would re-derive from `unknown` and lose it

forbidRelationships.note: THE DEFECT: binding to the rival class the file never imports
THE PRE-FIX SHAPE: no owner at all, leaving the store to the name model
A cast must NOT be re-derived as an instantiation; its evidence class is `cast`
